transcript:
Meeting header: 2027-10-22 16:00 UTC | Duration: ~48m
Attendees: Sofia Martinez (Redwood AE), Liam Chen (Redwood SE), Priya Kapoor (Redwood Product), Ethan Park (AuroraCloud PM), Maya Singh (AuroraCloud SA), Jules Laurent (AuroraCloud Security)

Auto-summary: quick sync to finalize marketplace packaging, reference architecture artifacts, and joint solution milestones. Main open items: 1-click deploy spec, terraform module, compliance docs, marketing assets, timeline for joint demo.

00:00:00 - Sofia Martinez: hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick round robin, and we'll jump into the marketplace checklist.
00:00:18 - Ethan Park: hi, Ethan here, glad to be on. we want to make sure AuroraCloud listing aligns with our portal and we can support redwood's one click flow.
00:00:28 - Maya Singh: Maya, integrations SA, i'll own the test account and deployment variables.
00:00:34 - Jules Laurent: Jules (security), i'll cover compliance Qs, encryption and KMS.
00:00:40 - Liam Chen: Liam from redwood eng, i'll go through reference arch suggestions and terraform snippets.
00:00:48 - Priya Kapoor: priya, product, focusing on co-marketing and listing copy.

00:01:05 - Sofia Martinez: objective for today: agree on what goes into the marketplace listing vs reference arch vs joint solution brief, and set owners & dates. also want to surface any blockers for auroracloud private deployments or org-level approvals.

00:02:22 - Liam Chen: quick technical note — for 1-click deploy we recommend providing either a terraform module or a cloudformation/arm template. our marketplace supports a few variants; terraform is easiest for customers and for us to automate smoke tests. when folks say 1-click what we do under the hood is a terraform apply against a customer-managed account or a marketplace deploy that spins up an AMI/cluster.
00:02:53 - Maya Singh: okay terraform sounds good. question: does redwood require a specific network layout? we have customers using both shared-vpc and dedicated vpc patterns.
00:03:08 - Liam Chen: we generally recommend a dedicated VPC per deployment for latency isolation, with peering or private link options. reference arch should show both: dedicated VPC with NAT/NGW and a shared VPC variant. also call out KV cache requirements — sorry KV cache, but transcription often says KV cash — it needs sticky storage for the model cache, and that affects throughput.
00:03:37 - Jules Laurent: on encryption — we need to confirm KMS integration points. do you expect customer-managed CMKs or will redwood manage keys for the marketplace listing?
00:03:49 - Sofia Martinez: for marketplace we'll support customer-managed KMS as best practice; the listing should call out KMS optionality and also the private deployment where customers must supply CMK. for hosted offering we have Redwood-managed KMS but for auroracloud marketplace we want CMS keys to be customer-provided.
00:04:10 - Ethan Park: perfect, we'll include a step in our security review to confirm CMK flow.

00:05:00 - Speaker 1: quick meta question — what about billing integration? marketplace handles purchase flow but how do we wire metering to the redwood backend?
00:05:12 - Priya Kapoor: good call — for marketplace listing we usually include deployment metadata and a connector that exchanges a short-lived token so redwood can register the deployment and meter usage back to the account. need to document API endpoints and token rotation.
00:05:33 - Maya Singh: ok, so we need example API calls, and a client secret rotation plan.
00:05:41 - Liam Chen: we'll add a small sample script in the terraform module that calls the registration endpoint post-deploy. it will use an initial marketplace token and then rotate. note: some partners require that the initial registration step is optional for air-gapped customers; we should call that out.

00:06:50 - Sofia Martinez: switching to the reference architecture doc — liam, can you walk through the things you think must be in the doc?
00:07:02 - Liam Chen: sure. core sections: 1) high-level diagram (redwood runtime, model variants, inference nodes), 2) network & security (VPC, subnets, security groups, private link), 3) storage & caching (KV cache, prefix cache), 4) key management (CMK examples), 5) scaling & autoscaling hints for dedicated pools, 6) operational runbooks (logs, traces, metrics to export). also include a small appendix with terraform snippets for module inputs: instance types, gpus, region mapping.
00:07:40 - Ethan Park: is there any particular sequence length expectation for the kernel selection? we have customers worried about very long context tails that blow up cost.
00:07:52 - Liam Chen: great point — include a note that model compilation and kernel selection are sensitive to sequence length distribution, recommend token limits and batching policies. put a sample batching config that shows per-model defaults, and mention Redwood Optimize suggestions for quantization.
00:08:12 - Maya Singh: will the reference arch mention fallback policies? some customers need automatic fallback to smaller model variants if GPU capacity constrained.
00:08:20 - Liam Chen: yes, add smart routing/fallback as an optional component. small diagram for routing by latency/cost/region and a short policy example.

00:09:40 - Jules Laurent: from security POV we need audit log schema examples — API calls, token exchange logs, KMS access logs. can you include sample CloudTrail/GCP audit entries?
00:09:53 - Liam Chen: we can include example log snippets. we'll show a sample trace with token issuance, registration, inference request, and model fallback.

00:11:05 - Sofia Martinez: content & assets for listing — priya, what do you need from auroracloud?
00:11:12 - Priya Kapoor: we'll need logos (SVG/PNG), 2 screenshots of the integration flow, short one-liner and 3 bullet product benefits, pricing tier mapping, and a hero diagram. also a short blurb for marketplace search taxonomy: keywords like "LLM inference", "low-latency", "GPU dedicated".
00:11:40 - Ethan Park: logos and screenshots we can provide by end of week. question on licensing — do you expect marketplace customers to have a separate contract with redwood or will auroracloud re-sell?
00:11:55 - Sofia Martinez: marketplace purchase will create a direct Redwood subscription for usage-based billing; auroracloud may offer a managed service on top. if partner wants to resell, that's a separate channel conversation and additional procurement steps.

00:13:10 - Speaker 2: minor transcription glitch — earlier mention of "re-rolled" should be "rollouts" in the docs.

00:13:30 - Liam Chen: testing plan for the integration: smoke test (deploy + registration), functional test (inference basic prompts), perf test (latency/throughput benchmarks), security scan. suggested perf harness: 30m run with mixed length token distribution to validate batching and KV cache behavior. we'll provide a benchmark spreadsheet template.
00:14:00 - Maya Singh: sounds good. for perf test do you have recommended instance types? we want to map to auroracloud sku names.
00:14:12 - Liam Chen: we'll include a mapping table: gtx-equivalents / a100 / h100 equivalents and sample instance sizes. also include quantization recommendations if customers want to lower cost.

00:15:30 - Jules Laurent: what level of SOC2 evidence do you need for marketplace approval? we can provide a broad extract but some customers require full report redaction.
00:15:42 - Sofia Martinez: for listing we need confirmation of SOC2 type II and an attestation. for private deployments we might need a copy of the report during procurement. in the immediate step, a redacted SOC2 + network diagram will suffice to start the listing security review.

00:17:05 - Ethan Park: on co-marketing and joint solution — priya, what's the timeline?
00:17:13 - Priya Kapoor: we'd like to have a one-pager + solution brief ready at launch. timeline: listing assets due 2027-10-27, reference arch by 2027-10-29, then joint demo week of 2027-11-08 and public listing targeted 2027-11-15 if approvals are smooth.
00:17:36 - Maya Singh: realistic for us. we may need to push if security docs take longer, but we'll try.

00:18:55 - Speaker 3: quick clarifying Q — for private deployment pattern (VPC/on-prem), what does the control plane look like? does auroracloud host agent or does redwood offer an air-gapped bundle?
00:19:07 - Liam Chen: Redwood offers both: a control plane can be either Redwood-managed with private link to the customer env, or customers can run a customer-managed control plane. for air-gapped on-prem we provide an on-prem package (installer + policies) and a curated image. include that matrix in the reference arch doc.
00:19:29 - Jules Laurent: we need the on-prem installer SHA and attestations for image provenance.
00:19:35 - Sofia Martinez: we'll include checksums and a short note on image signing. Liam will add the details.

00:20:50 - Ethan Park: about the marketplace listing page — any constraints on copy/claims? like latency numbers?
00:20:59 - Priya Kapoor: keep public claims conservative; include typical latencies with disclaimers referencing region and instance type. for per-token costs we show ranges and call out that exact cost depends on model and config. also include a link to the Redwood Optimize recommendations.

00:22:10 - Liam Chen: minor tech note: reference arch should note that compilation and kernel selection vary across hardware, so provide recommended kernel sets per region/hardware in the appendix.

00:23:45 - Sofia Martinez: ok let's recap decisions: terraform module + 1-click terraform flow, reference arch with dedicated & shared VPC patterns, KMS = customer-managed by default, include audit log examples, provide benchmark template and mapping table for instance SKUs, and provide marketplace assets. owners assigned.

00:24:12 - Ethan Park: question about rollouts — how do canaries/A-B work with marketplace deployments?
00:24:24 - Liam Chen: the runtime supports canary and A/B via routing policies. for marketplace we recommend a staged rollout: deploy to a sandbox -> canary 5-10% traffic -> full. document the rollback steps in the runbook.

00:25:50 - Maya Singh: we'll need a runbook excerpt for our SREs.
00:25:58 - Liam Chen: we'll attach a runbook excerpt to the reference arch doc.

00:27:10 - Speaker 4: small note — some customers ask for private testing environment that keeps data in region. do you support region pinning?
00:27:21 - Sofia Martinez: yes, region pinning is supported; include region options in the listing and reference arch.

00:28:40 - Priya Kapoor: marketing collateral: priya to draft one-pager once assets in. redwood will draft joint press paragraph and auroracloud to review. aim to align announcement after listing goes live.

00:30:05 - Jules Laurent: security follow-up: i'll compile a short Q/A doc with expected artifacts, encryption flow, and sample logs. will drop to the shared folder.

00:30:38 - Liam Chen: one more technical gotcha — some partners run Kubernetes autoscaler that kills warm caches; call that out because it impacts KV cache warm-up and latency. propose a small note in ops hints: pin a minimum replica count during warm-up.
00:30:59 - Maya Singh: good catch, we'll test that pattern.

00:32:10 - Sofia Martinez: any blockers we're missing?
00:32:18 - Ethan Park: none immediate, just dependencies on the SOC2 extract and a short legal review.
00:32:26 - Jules Laurent: legal will need the SLA template if we pursue a co-sell route; not necessary for marketplace listing.

00:33:40 - Priya Kapoor: timeline check again: owners noted — if everyone hits dates we'll target listing 2027-11-15.

00:35:00 - Speaker 5: small audio hiccup, sorry if that repeated.

00:35:20 - Liam Chen: ok final technical deliverables list: terraform module + sample vars file, reference architecture PDF (with diagrams), runbook excerpt, benchmark spreadsheet, example log snippets, and a smoke test script. we'll push to the shared repo.
00:35:48 - Maya Singh: i'll provision a test tenant and grant redwood access to run smoke tests.

00:36:20 - Sofia Martinez: cool — let's confirm distribution: redwood will upload artifacts to the shared folder and ping auroracloud; auroracloud will upload SOC2 + logos. then we'll schedule the joint demo.

00:37:05 - Ethan Park: one last Q on support model: post-listing how are support tickets triaged?
00:37:14 - Sofia Martinez: marketplace customers open a support ticket with redwood; auroracloud can also escalate to redwood via partner channel. document will include support flow and SLAs.

00:38:40 - Priya Kapoor: action items recap on the call, repeating owners and due dates.

00:39:02 - Sofia Martinez: great, thank you everyone. we'll follow up with the docs and schedule the enablement.

00:39:20 - Ethan Park: thanks all.

00:39:28 - Maya Singh: thanks.

00:39:34 - Jules Laurent: bye.

00:39:40 - End of recording.

Notes on transcript quality: approximate timestamps, occasional transcription errors (KV cash, re-rolled -> rollouts). References to internal artifacts: shared repo link (placeholder: https://redwood.internal/shared/auroracloud-marketplace), benchmark spreadsheet (placeholder: https://redwood.internal/benchmarks/auroracloud-template.xlsx).

Attachments/links mentioned: https://redwood.internal/shared/auroracloud-marketplace (docs + terraform), https://redwood.internal/benchmarks/auroracloud-template.xlsx (perf template).

Final recap (plain): Owners and due dates: Sofia - listing copy 10/27; Liam - reference arch + terraform 10/29; Maya - test account 10/31; Jules - SOC2 artifacts 11/03; Priya+Ethan - demo week of 11/08. Target public listing: 11/15 pending approvals.
